description.value: Hike-in backcountry campsite at an alpine lake deep in E.C. Manning Park's Cascade Mountains; a permit is required ($5/person/night) but no advance reservation, and the site is unreachable by any road or loaded bike.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record identifies Poland Lake Campground as a BC Parks backcountry camp_site within E.C. Manning Park. The website confirms Poland Lake is one of the listed backcountry campgrounds on the park's backcountry camping page. The website explicitly states that only Buckhorn, Kicking Horse, and Frosty Creek require reservations during peak season — Poland Lake is not among them — and that 'most backcountry campgrounds in E.C. Manning Park do not accept reservations,' providing clear negative evidence for reservations. No campground-specific amenity details (water, shelter, food storage, etc.) are provided for Poland Lake on this page.
concerns: Website URL points to the general E.C. Manning Park backcountry camping overview page rather than a Poland Lake-specific page; no campground-level amenity details (water, food storage, shelter) are available from this source.
No address or phone number in OSM record; coordinates are the only locator.
Website notes the park has no cellphone service — cyclists should be aware permits must be arranged before arrival or in person at the visitor centre or lodge.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Poland Lake Campground is an active, legitimate BC Parks backcountry campsite in E.C. Manning Park accessible to touring cyclists; it is a genuine overnight destination with a required permit process and would be a useful listing for cyclists undertaking backcountry routes.
enrichment_extras.notes: A backcountry permit (not a reservation) is required for all overnight stays at Poland Lake. Permits can be registered at camping.bcparks.ca, by calling 1-800-689-9025, or in person at the Manning Park visitor centre, Manning Park Lodge, or Lightning Lake gatehouse.
